description_full: Post Holdings, Inc. operates as a consumer packaged goods holding company in the United States and internationally. It operates through four segments: Post Consumer Brands, Foodservice, Refrigerated Retail, and Weetabix. The Post Consumer Brands segment manufactures, markets, and sells branded and private label ready-to-eat (RTE) cereals under Honey Bunches of Oats, Pebbles, and Malt-O-Meal brands; hot cereal; peanut butter under the Peter Pan brand; and branded and private label pet food under Rachael Ray Nutrish, Nature's Recipe, 9Lives, Kibbles 'n Bits and Gravy Train brands. Its Foodservice segment produces and distributes egg products primarily under Papetti's and Abbotsford Farms brands, as well as potato products in the foodservice and food ingredient channels. This segment also manufactures certain meat products. The Refrigerated Retail segment produces and distributes side dish, potato, sausage products under Bob Evans, Bob Evans Farms, and Simply Potatoes brands; eggs and egg products under Bob Evans Egg Whites and Egg Beaters brands; and cheese and other dairy products under Crystal Farms brand. Its Weetabix segment manufactures, markets, and distributes branded and private label RTE cereal under Weetabix and Alpen brands; hot cereals and other cereal-based food products; private label cereals; and protein-based shakes under the UFIT brand, and nutritional snacks. It serves grocery stores, mass merchandise customers, supercenters, club stores, natural/specialty stores, dollar stores, discounters, wholesalers, convenience stores, pet supply retailers, drug store customers, foodservice distributors, and national restaurant chains, as well as sells its products in the military, ecommerce, and foodservice channels. The company was founded in 1895 and is headquartered in Saint Louis, Missouri.

financial_summary: Post Holdings, Inc. is a mid-cap consumer defensive business with a $3.7B market cap on $8.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +12% over the past three years and +5% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 6% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 30%.

The business throws off $563M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.02× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 5.2× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 16% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
